title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: pricing and rounding of the final detention line
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category fixes how the billed detention days of a per-container record are priced and combined into the amount of its final detention line.

## Rule

1. Each detention day is billed at the detention rate of its slab and of the container's rate class for the product on the record.
2. Detention days carry no dangerous-goods uplift, whatever the cargo type of the booking.
3. The day rates are added up, and only the sum is rounded to the cent.

## The amount in words

The detention amount is the slab 1 days multiplied by the slab 1 detention rate, plus in the same way the slab 2, slab 3 and slab 4 days each multiplied by their own rate, all for the rate class and the product on the record, with the total then rounded to the cent once.

## Worked example (hypothetical detention rates of USD 10.00, 20.00, 30.00 and 40.00 per day, used only for illustration)

A detention line has 2 days in slab 2 and 5 days in slab 3. The amount is 2 days multiplied by USD 20.00, that is USD 40.00, together with 5 days multiplied by USD 30.00, that is USD 150.00: USD 190.00 in total.

## Wrong reading and correct basis

| Wrong reading | Correct basis |
|---|---|
| "The container is on a dangerous-goods booking, so the detention rates are raised too." | Detention days carry no dangerous-goods uplift. |
| "Each day is rounded before the days are added." | The day rates are added first and only the sum is rounded to the cent. |
